input.rationale: XRD on four compositions spread across the library showed the same main phase everywhere: a dominant peak at Q≈2.79 with minor peaks at 3.21, 4.55 and 5.34 Å⁻¹. The only exception was a small extra reflection at Q≈1.16 in the Ca-rich corner. So I used the three merit measurements on the Co-rich (21), Mn-rich (146) and Ca-rich (43) corners. None gave a positive photocurrent under 2.72 eV light: 21 = -6e-8 A, 146 = 0.0 A, 43 = -1.5e-7 A. Index 146 (Mn-rich) has the highest measured merit. It is the least negative value, not a real positive photoresponse.

rejected.reason: Co-rich corner gave a slightly negative photocurrent (-6e-8 A)
Ca-rich corner, which has an extra low-Q phase, gave the most negative photocurrent (-1.5e-7 A)

content.text:
None of the three compositions I measured gave a real positive photocurrent, so this campaign didn't find a working photoanode. I submitted index 146 (Ca 0.15, Co 0.21, Mn 0.64) as best because it read 0.0 A, while the other two were negative.

| Index | Region | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 146 | Mn-rich | 0.0 |
| 21 | Co-rich | -6e-8 |
| 43 | Ca-rich | -1.5e-7 |

- **XRD first:** I used 4 of the 5 XRD scans on points spread across the library. The same main phase showed up everywhere. The only difference was a small extra peak at Q≈1.16 Å⁻¹ in the Ca-rich corner (index 43). So XRD didn't point to a promising region.
- **Merit measurements:** With only 3, I measured one point in each corner. The first two (Co-rich and Mn-rich) both came out at about zero, so there was no trend to follow. I spent the last one on the Ca-rich corner because it had the different phase, and it gave the most negative reading.

The middle of the composition range was never measured, so a better composition could still be there.
